slot.brief: Show x(t) or v(t) graphs of several candidates and identify which represents SHM, or read off amplitude/frequency/phase from a given SHM curve.

stem: The displacement–time curve of a particle is shown in the figure. Which equation of motion is consistent with the graph?

verdicts.working: The graph has amplitude 4 cm and period 4 s, so ω = 2π/T = π/2. At t = 0, x = 2 cm and the slope is negative, giving phase π/3. Thus x(t) = 4 cos(πt/2 + π/3) cm.

working:
$A=4\ \text{cm},\quad T=4\ \text{s}\Rightarrow \omega=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$
$x(0)=2\ \text{cm}\Rightarrow \cos\phi=\dfrac12$; initial slope is negative, so $\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
$x(t)=4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\ \text{cm}$

Independent check: The graph has amplitude 4 cm and period 4 s, so ω = 2π/T = π/2. At t = 0, x = 2 cm and the slope is negative, giving phase π/3. Thus x(t) = 4 cos(πt/2 + π/3) cm.
solution:
From the graph, $A=4\,\text{cm}$ and $T=4\,\text{s}$, so $\omega=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\text{s}^{-1}$.
At $t=0$, $x=2\,\text{cm}$, hence $\cos\phi=\dfrac{1}{2}$; the negative initial slope gives $\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
$$x(t)=4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\text{cm}$$

draft.stem: The displacement–time curve of a particle is shown in the figure. Which equation of motion is consistent with the graph?

figure.description: Draw a displacement–time graph with horizontal axis labeled $t$ (s), running from $0$ to $4$, and vertical axis labeled $x$ (cm). Mark horizontal ticks at $0$, $\dfrac{1}{3}$, $\dfrac{4}{3}$, $\dfrac{7}{3}$, $\dfrac{10}{3}$ and $4$; mark vertical ticks at $-4$, $0$, $2$ and $4$. Draw a smooth wave-shaped curve starting at $(0,2)$ and initially descending; it crosses $x=0$ at $t=\dfrac{1}{3}$, reaches a minimum at $(\dfrac{4}{3},-4)$, crosses $x=0$ again at $t=\dfrac{7}{3}$, reaches a maximum at $(\dfrac{10}{3},4)$, and ends at $(4,2)$ while descending.

draft.working:

$x(0)=2\ \text{cm}\Rightarrow \cos\phi=\dfrac12$; initial slope is negative, so $\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
$x(t)=4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\ \text{cm}$
